topicTitle: Patterns and volume of world trade

questions.topicTitle: Patterns and volume of world trade
questions.stem: Which of the following best defines the pattern of trade?
options: The composition and direction of a country's trade: what it trades and with whom
The total value of a country's exports
The balance between a country's exports and imports
The rate at which a country's trade is growing
questions.why: Pattern concerns composition and direction, not size or balance.
whyNot: That is export value.
That is the trade balance.
That is trade growth.

questions.topicTitle: Patterns and volume of world trade
questions.stem: Which of the following best defines the volume of trade?
options: The quantity of goods and services traded, measured independently of price changes
The money value of goods and services traded
The number of countries a nation trades with
The weight of goods shipped in a period
questions.why: Volume is quantity; value is quantity multiplied by price. The distinction carries marks in data questions.
whyNot: That is the value of trade.
That is the number of trading partners.
Weight is one physical measure, not the economic definition.

questions.topicTitle: Patterns and volume of world trade
questions.stem: Which region gained the largest share of world manufacturing over recent decades?
options: Asia
Western Europe
Sub-Saharan Africa
South America
questions.why: Low labour costs, improving infrastructure and large-scale investment made Asia the location for assembly and then for more sophisticated production.
whyNot: Western Europe's share fell.
Its share of world manufacturing remains small.
Its share did not grow comparably.

questions.topicTitle: Patterns and volume of world trade
questions.stem: Which of the following best defines a bilateral trade agreement?
options: A trade agreement between two countries reducing barriers between them
An agreement among all WTO members
An agreement between a country and a trading bloc
An agreement to fix exchange rates between two currencies
questions.why: Bilateral and regional deals now account for most new liberalisation, since multilateral negotiation has stalled.
whyNot: That would be a multilateral agreement.
That is a country-to-bloc agreement, a related but different form.
That is a monetary arrangement.

questions.topicTitle: Patterns and volume of world trade
questions.stem: How did the growth of emerging economies change commodity trade flows?
options: Commodity exporters found their largest customers were no longer in the developed world
Demand for commodities fell as emerging economies industrialised
Commodity prices became permanently stable
Commodity exports were replaced entirely by services
questions.why: Industrialisation and construction require metals, energy and food, which redirected flows and not just their size.
whyNot: Industrialisation raises commodity demand sharply.
Commodity prices remained highly volatile.
Commodity exports continued to grow.

questions.topicTitle: Patterns and volume of world trade
questions.stem: What is the ladder pattern in changing comparative advantage?
options: Each cohort of industrialising economies moves up as the next takes over the lowest-value work
Countries move down the value chain as they develop
All countries specialise in the same goods over time
Comparative advantage is fixed once established
questions.why: Wage growth in an industrialising country pushes its advantage towards higher-value production, and lower-cost countries take over assembly.
whyNot: Development moves countries up, not down, the value chain.
Specialisation patterns continue to differ.
It moves with wages, education, technology and exchange rates.

questions.topicTitle: Patterns and volume of world trade
questions.stem: How do trading blocs change the pattern rather than the volume of trade?
options: Trade becomes more regional as firms source within the bloc rather than from the cheapest world supplier
Blocs prevent all trade with non-members
Blocs reduce the total volume of world trade to zero
Blocs have no effect on where goods are sourced
questions.why: That is trade diversion, and the geographic pattern shifts even where the total does not.
whyNot: Trade with non-members continues, subject to the external tariff.
Blocs generally raise total trade.
The external tariff directly changes sourcing decisions.

questions.topicTitle: Patterns and volume of world trade
questions.stem: Why is a country whose competitiveness rests on a weak currency not genuinely more competitive?
options: The exchange rate changes trade flows without changing underlying costs or productivity
A weak currency has no effect on export prices
Weak currencies are always accompanied by low productivity
Exchange rates are fixed by the WTO
questions.why: Inflation will typically erode the advantage over time, so the effect on the pattern of trade is temporary.
whyNot: It lowers export prices in foreign currency directly.
The two are not necessarily linked.
The WTO does not set exchange rates.

questions.topicTitle: Patterns and volume of world trade
questions.stem: Which two effects of protectionism on trade should be distinguished?
options: Trade reduction, lowering the total traded, and trade redirection, shifting it to another partner
Trade creation and trade diversion
Volume and value
Exports and imports
questions.why: Recent tariff increases between major economies produced mainly redirection: goods were rerouted through third countries rather than not traded at all.
whyNot: Those are the effects of bloc formation, not protection generally.
That is a measurement distinction rather than an effect.
Those are the two sides of trade, not two effects.

questions.topicTitle: Patterns and volume of world trade
questions.stem: Why did trade grow faster than world output for several decades?
options: Falling barriers and transport costs, plus the fragmentation of production into supply chains
World output stopped growing entirely
Trade statistics began to include domestic sales
Countries stopped consuming their own production
questions.why: A single finished good crosses borders several times in a fragmented supply chain and is counted at each border, which inflates recorded trade.
whyNot: Output grew throughout; trade simply grew faster.
Trade statistics record cross-border transactions.
Domestic consumption remains the largest component of demand.

questions.topicTitle: Patterns and volume of world trade
questions.stem: Why did trade in services grow faster than trade in goods?
options: Cheap reliable communication made software, design, finance and support tradable
Services became physically easier to ship
Tariffs on services were always higher
Demand for goods fell in absolute terms
questions.why: Tourism and education also grew with rising incomes, adding to the shift towards services.
whyNot: Services are not shipped; they are delivered electronically.
Services remained less liberalised, which held the growth back rather than driving it.
Goods trade continued to grow.

questions.topicTitle: Patterns and volume of world trade
questions.stem: A commodity exporter's export value rises while its export volume falls. What has happened?
options: Prices have risen faster than quantities have fallen
Quantities have risen faster than prices have fallen
The exchange rate has been fixed
The data must be inconsistent
questions.why: This is exactly what happens during a commodity price boom, and noticing it earns credit in a data question.
whyNot: That would raise volume, not reduce it.
Exchange rate policy does not explain the divergence.
Value and volume routinely move differently.

questions.topicTitle: Patterns and volume of world trade
questions.stem: Which recent change suggests the growth of trade relative to output is not automatic?
options: Supply chains have been shortened as firms prioritise resilience over cost
Communication costs have started to rise
Containerisation has been abandoned
The WTO has raised all members' tariffs
questions.why: Rising barriers and a preference for resilience slowed, and in some periods reversed, the growth of trade relative to output.
whyNot: Communication costs have continued to fall.
Container shipping remains the dominant mode.
The WTO does not set members' tariffs.

questions.topicTitle: Patterns and volume of world trade
options: Trade between developing and emerging economies
Trade between countries in the southern hemisphere only
Trade in primary products only
Trade conducted in a single currency
questions.why: It was historically small and is now substantial, which is one of the major changes in the pattern of world trade.
whyNot: It refers to development status rather than geography.
It covers manufactures and services too.
Currency is not part of the definition.

questions.topicTitle: Patterns and volume of world trade
questions.stem: In a data question on trade flows, what should be done first?
options: Describe the change accurately, with direction, size and period, quoting the figures
State the recommendation before analysing the data
Explain all five influences on trade patterns
Calculate the terms of trade
questions.why: Accurate description comes first, then the volume-against-value check, then two or three reasons matched to the evidence.
whyNot: A conclusion before analysis is unsupported.
Two or three selected influences beat all five superficially.
Only if the data supports it and the question asks.

questions.topicTitle: Patterns and volume of world trade
questions.stem: Which of the following is a structural rather than temporary cause of a change in trade patterns?
options: A change in comparative advantage through education and technology
A movement in the exchange rate
A one-year commodity price spike
A temporary export licensing delay
questions.why: Distinguishing structural from temporary causes is what allows a judgement about whether the change will persist.
whyNot: Exchange rate movements are typically temporary in their effect.
A price spike is by definition temporary.
Administrative delay is short-lived.
